title: Extremal and global-time statistics of sluggish random walks with stochastic resetting
abstract: We study the extremal and global-time statistics of a one-dimensional sluggish random walk, whose diffusivity decays as a power law of the distance from the origin, under Poissonian resetting to the origin. A change of variable maps the process onto a signed Bessel process, so that renewal theory applies. We obtain the exact Laplace transform of the distribution of the maximum over a finite window. At long times the centered maximum of the transformed process follows the Gumbel law, and in physical space the typical maximum grows as a power of the logarithm of the window length. The far-tail rate function does not depend on $α$ in the Bessel variable, so the second-order dynamical transition known for Brownian resetting, between maxima produced by a single anomalously long inter-reset interval and maxima produced by an interval occupying essentially the whole window, holds for every $α$. The time of the maximum is uniformly distributed in the bulk of the window, with boundary layers that shift its mean above the midpoint logarithmically in the window length. The last-passage time through the origin has an exact density, and the time elapsed since it converges to a Gamma law. Reflection symmetry makes the occupation time of the positive half-line and the last-passage time uncorrelated. The results reduce to the Brownian case and agree with simulations.
summary: This paper analyzes the extreme statistics of a sluggish random walk whose movement is hindered by position-dependent diffusivity and periodically reset to the origin. By mapping the process to a Bessel process, the authors derive that the maximum value follows Gumbel statistics at long times. The results provide exact scaling laws for the maximum and global times, extending known results from simple Brownian motion to more complex, non-uniform diffusion regimes.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the extremal and global-time statistics of a one-dimensional sluggish random walk subjected to stochastic resetting at the origin.
main_result: The maximum of the process follows the Gumbel law at long times, and the typical maximum scales as a power of the logarithm of the window length, regardless of the diffusivity decay parameter $\alpha$.
method: The analysis employs renewal theory after mapping the sluggish walk to a signed Bessel process, utilizing Laplace transforms and pole identification in the complex plane for long-time asymptotics.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional random walk where the diffusivity decays as a power law $D(x) = |x|^{-\alpha}$, coupled with Poissonian resetting to the origin. This leads to a PDE solved via mapping to a signed Bessel process.
key_observables: Maximum value ($M_T$), time of maximum ($t_M$), and last-passage time through the origin ($t_l$).
important_parameters: Diffusivity decay exponent $\alpha$, resetting rate $r$, and observation window length $T$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a Poissonian resetting process and utilizes the continuum limit PDE formulation for the walk.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes reference Figure 2 for comparison with simulations.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by mapping the sluggish walk to a Bessel process, deriving the Laplace transform of the maximum distribution using renewal theory, and analyzing the long-time limits for the maximum, time of maximum, and last-passage time.
why_interesting: The techniques developed for analyzing extreme value statistics in non-Markovian, non-stationary processes (like sluggish walks) under external driving (resetting) are highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in complex quantum systems.
